ports.note: Takes a point layer of cases, each with a date, and gives back the clusters it reports as circles: one polygon per cluster, carrying its days, places, observed and expected cases, likelihood ratio and p-value.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no mapping to an external vocabulary. fw:SpaceTimeScan and fw:ScanCluster are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties. The receipt names the date column, the unit, the study period, every record not scanned and why, the limits, the replications, the seed and the random stream, and every cluster reported with its counts and p-value.

changes.description: Places within 10 cm of the same distance from a centre join a circle together, and distances are measured from each place's recorded coordinates, not from their 6-decimal rounding. Ties were exact to a millionth of a millimetre, so rounding noise decided which equidistant houses tied: moving Hagelloch 3.7 km west (its anchor corrected, 2026-11-10), which changes no distance, changed one circle and one p-value. Now the circles are the same wherever the village sits (1,307 for Hagelloch at every position tried). Hagelloch's clusters and its first day flagged, 21 November 1861, are unchanged; the 21 November p-value is 0.039, was 0.041.
